---
title: "Glossary"
subtitle: "Causal inference terms, cross-linked to each other"
toc: false
jupyter: python3
---

This page is generated from `_glossary.yml` — the same file the
`{{{< term key >}}}` shortcode reads for hover definitions in the chapters. A
definition lives in one place, so there is nowhere for it to drift.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis

from pathlib import Path

import yaml
from IPython.display import Markdown, display

data = yaml.safe_load(Path("_glossary.yml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
entries = data["glossary"]

# Alphabetical by the visible term rather than by key: readers scan labels.
for key, e in sorted(entries.items(), key=lambda kv: kv[1].get("term", kv[0]).lower()):
    out = [f'### {e.get("term", key)} {{#term-{key}}}\n']
    if e.get("short"):
        out.append(f'*{e["short"]}*\n')
    if e.get("def"):
        out.append(e["def"].strip() + "\n")
    # Other names for the same object. Reading across literatures is where
    # most of the confusion in this field comes from.
    if e.get("aka"):
        out.append(f'\nAlso called: {e["aka"].strip()}\n')
    # A real disagreement between standard works, called out rather than
    # silently resolved.
    if e.get("note"):
        out.append(f'\n::: {{.callout-warning appearance="simple"}}\n'
                   f'{e["note"].strip()}\n:::\n')
    # Citekeys become live citations: the reference list at the bottom of the
    # page is assembled by citeproc, not maintained by hand.
    if e.get("src"):
        cites = "; ".join(f"@{k}" for k in e["src"])
        out.append(f"\nSource: [{cites}]\n")
    if e.get("see"):
        links = ", ".join(
            f'[{entries.get(k, {}).get("term", k)}](#term-{k})' for k in e["see"]
        )
        out.append(f"\nSee also: {links}\n")
    display(Markdown("\n".join(out)))
```

---

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Missing a term? Add an entry to `_glossary.yml` and it appears here and in
hover tooltips across the site. A link to a key that does not exist still
renders, but drops a warning in the build log — a reminder to write the
definition, not a build failure.
:::
